name: Tonelux Tilt Live
comparative_edge: Choose Live over standard Tilt for stage monitors or any path where tonal rebalancing must obey a strict maximum boost. Standard Tilt retains modeled transformer color and normal makeup Gain; Equalizers remains better for corrective work or a movable center.

advanced_moves.setup: On a wedge-monitor bus, set Boost Ceiling to minimum before moving Tilt or Loud away from center.
advanced_moves.action: Create the needed balance using attenuation-only curves, then raise Boost Ceiling only if additional apparent clarity is required and feedback margin is known.
advanced_moves.listen_for: The mix should rebalance without any frequency becoming louder than bypass; stop raising the ceiling if ringing or feedback margin worsens.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: At minimum, Boost Ceiling offsets the curve so its highest point is 0 dB while preserving the Tilt or Loud shape below it.

advanced_moves.setup: For in-ear monitoring, start with Boost Ceiling at its full in-ear position and a neutral Tilt.
advanced_moves.action: Make small broad changes for fatigue, then lower the ceiling until perceived balance remains but peaks no longer rise unnecessarily.
advanced_moves.listen_for: Clarity should improve without the entire monitor feed seeming louder; compare after enough time for ear-fatigue judgment, not one transient.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: The ceiling continuously interpolates between normal ±6 dB behavior and cut-only operation, allowing the same curve at lower maximum gain.

use_cases.application: Use a cut-only Tilt to reduce warmth and expose intelligibility without boosting the feedback-prone top end.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: Boost Ceiling turns a familiar tilt gesture into an attenuation-only response suitable for limited stage gain-before-feedback.

use_cases.context: Electronic live set — Performer in-ear mix
use_cases.application: Use restrained Loud mode to manage apparent closeness as fatigue develops, then cap the maximum boost below the standard response.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: It permits a global monitoring adjustment without revisiting many individual channel EQs during performance.

pairings.goal: Precise cleanup plus Tonelux Tilt Live's broad character in one reorderable EQ environment.
pairings.order: Equalizers Modern → Tonelux Tilt Live in the Vintage slot
pairings.setup: Create only the necessary modern cuts or dynamic bands, load Tonelux Tilt Live, then compare M→V with V→M at matched output.
pairings.why_it_works: Modern bands add narrow or dynamic control around the constrained model. Order becomes audible when dynamics or level-dependent model behavior makes the stages non-commutative.
pairings.caution: With static linear stages, reversing order may make no audible difference; do not invent one. Re-check level whenever dynamics or modeled saturation is active.

insider_note: Documented behavior: Tilt Live omits standard Tilt's transformer modeling to preserve DSP power and replaces output Gain with Boost Ceiling. It is therefore not merely the same sound with an added safety control.
avoid_when: Avoid it when transformer color is part of the goal, when makeup gain is needed inside the plugin, or when a narrow feedback mode must be notched.

sources.title: Softube Tonelux Tilt and Tilt Live user manual

name: Weiss EQ1
comparative_edge: Choose it over Equalizers when you need Weiss's exact hardware-code lineage, true linear-phase operation, selectable dithering, or expansion as well as compression per band. Choose Equalizers for a vintage insert stage and lighter everyday sidechain workflow; choose Weiss EQ MP when static minimum-phase mixing is enough.

advanced_moves.setup: On a kick or transient whose desirable attack appears only on strong hits, enter DYN mode, create a peaking boost, and choose an expansion Ratio below 1:1.
advanced_moves.action: Set Threshold so only featured hits cross it, use Boost as the maximum enhancement, then tune Attack/Release to follow the envelope without chatter.
advanced_moves.listen_for: Strong hits should gain definition while quieter ones retain their original balance; reject settings that make ambience or bleed trigger the lift.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: Expansion ratios move gain upward above threshold, with Boost limiting the maximum dynamic change.

advanced_moves.setup: For a static mastering correction, create the same curve in DYN minimum-phase and LP modes, with all dynamics disabled and output matched.
advanced_moves.action: Audition on attacks and low-frequency transitions, then retain LP only if reduced phase shift outweighs pre-ringing and roughly 250 ms latency.
advanced_moves.listen_for: LP may sound cleaner on sustained material but can soften or precede sharp events; decide from transients, not the graph.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: The two modes are different architectures: LP uses lookahead to remove phase shift, while DYN is lower-latency minimum phase.

use_cases.application: Compare a restrained static curve in LP and DYN modes, choosing from transient behavior and stereo depth rather than assuming LP wins.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: It provides both verified Weiss linear-phase and minimum-phase paths in one instance with detailed mastering metering.

use_cases.application: Use a dynamic expansion band to enhance only the strongest kick or snare attacks, with Boost setting a hard maximum lift.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: Its variable expansion ratios extend beyond ordinary dynamic-EQ attenuation and can be run with low dynamic latency.

pairings.goal: Remove narrow or dynamic excess before adding tightly targeted mastering harmonics.
pairings.order: Weiss EQ1 → Weiss Exciter
pairings.setup: Solve resonances or level-dependent harshness in EQ1 DYN mode, then define Exciter Pre/Post bands around the remaining useful source range.
pairings.why_it_works: Correction prevents unwanted peaks from seeding new harmonics; Exciter then adds overtones in a parallel, frequency-bounded path rather than restoring brightness with another EQ boost.
pairings.caution: Match phase modes and account for EQ1 latency. Excess correction can leave the exciter generating harmonics from an unnaturally hollow source.

insider_note: Documented behavior: low-latency DYN disables dynamics lookahead, while LP latency is typically around 250 ms. Low latency is a behavior trade-off, not just a host-reporting preference.
avoid_when: Avoid LP mode for tracking or rhythm-critical live paths, and avoid EQ1 altogether when seven static minimum-phase bands are all you need—EQ MP is simpler.

sources.title: Softube Weiss EQ1 user manual

name: Weiss EQ MP
comparative_edge: Choose EQ MP over EQ1 for faster static mix work with the same low-noise code and seven freely typed bands, without dynamic or linear-phase decisions. Choose Equalizers when sidechain dynamics or a vintage stage matters; choose a modeled analog EQ when its nonlinear constraints are the desired result.

advanced_moves.setup: On a mix bus, create the necessary high- or low-pass filter at the gentlest 6 dB/octave slope and solo its difference signal.
advanced_moves.action: Increase slope through 12, 24, 48, and 96 dB/octave only until unwanted content is removed; re-check un-soloed transients after every step.
advanced_moves.listen_for: The audible removed signal should contain the problem, not the source's timing or body; reject brickwall slopes that create an unnaturally detached edge.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: All seven bands can become minimum-phase cut filters with five documented slopes, and Solo auditions the processed difference.

advanced_moves.setup: Build a linked stereo curve first, then copy Channel 1 to Channel 2 before disengaging Ganged and entering M/S.
advanced_moves.action: Make one small Side-only correction while preserving the copied baseline, and use A/B states to compare against the fully linked version.
advanced_moves.listen_for: The stereo adjustment should solve a clear imbalance without moving the phantom center or changing mono tonality unexpectedly.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: Copy-before-ungang preserves identical starting states; otherwise the second channel may retain unrelated previous values.

use_cases.application: Use two or three static bands and the gentlest effective cuts, relying on difference Solo to verify that musical fundamentals remain.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: It keeps Weiss's low-noise static path without EQ1's mastering-mode overhead or an analog model's added nonlinearity.

use_cases.application: Copy linked settings, ungang in M/S, and make one Side-only low or upper-mid correction while monitoring mono.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: Seven equal bands and explicit channel-copy workflow support precise stereo repair without dynamic processing.

pairings.goal: Separate static spectral balance from additive harmonic brightness in a low-noise Weiss chain.
pairings.order: Weiss EQ MP → Weiss Exciter
pairings.setup: Finish broad balance and cuts in EQ MP, level-match, then target Exciter's input fundamentals and output harmonics without repeating the same shelf.
pairings.why_it_works: EQ MP establishes the source spectrum; Exciter can add new overtones with reduced fundamental leakage instead of creating more static EQ tilt.
pairings.caution: Do not use both processors to lift the same top region. Compare against EQ MP alone at matched loudness.

insider_note: Documented behavior: EQ MP runs the same code as EQ1 but removes mastering-specific use cases. Its cut filters are minimum phase even at the 96 dB/octave setting; it is not a hidden linear-phase mode.
avoid_when: Avoid it when a band must react to level, when true linear phase is required, or when analog-stage color is part of the assignment.

sources.title: Softube Weiss EQ MP user manual

name: Tape
comparative_edge: Choose Tape over Dirty Tape for controllable machine family, speed, crosstalk, and mastering-scale cohesion rather than overt damage. Choose Harmonics when transient reconstruction and distortion family matter more than tape motion; choose Overstayer M-A-S when peak bending without wow, noise, or tape bandwidth is the goal.

advanced_moves.setup: On a bus, set 15 or 30 ips, disable Noise, Stability modulation, and Crosstalk, then switch the VU meters to THD.
advanced_moves.action: For each Type, adjust Input and Amount to the same subtle THD reading and match Output before comparing. Add HF Trim only after selecting the machine behavior.
advanced_moves.listen_for: Compare transient rounding, low-frequency contour, and sustain at equal distortion and loudness; reject a type that wins only because it is hotter.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: The three tape types are input-dependent, and both Input and Amount change their color; matching THD and loudness reduces drive-level bias without pretending the harmonic spectra are identical.

advanced_moves.setup: On a stereo pad, echo, or backing-vocal return, select a stable Type and set Dry/Wet below full.
advanced_moves.action: Reduce Speed Stability until modulation becomes audible, then adjust Dry/Wet for deliberate chorus depth. Add Crosstalk separately and re-check mono before touching HF Trim.
advanced_moves.listen_for: Pitch motion should enlarge the return without pulling the dry center off pitch; mono should not reveal phasey thinning.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: Blending dry with a speed-varying tape path creates chorusing, while Crosstalk adds a separate left/right leakage mechanism.

use_cases.application: Compare Types at equal THD and output, use a higher speed for restrained transient control, then compensate only the high-frequency loss that remains.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: Tape exposes machine family, speed, THD, and HF compensation directly; Dirty Tape bundles those concerns into a degradation effect.

use_cases.application: Use partial Dry/Wet with slight instability for ensemble spread, then add restrained crosstalk and check mono.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: Its separately adjustable motion and stereo leakage can make a clean return feel recorded together without the overt dropouts of Dirty Tape.

pairings.goal: Remove drive-dominating excess before adding Tape.
pairings.order: Equalizers → Tape
pairings.setup: High-pass or make one restrained corrective cut first, level-match, then raise the color stage until the intended harmonics or peak bending appear.
pairings.why_it_works: Nonlinear processors respond to incoming level by frequency, so removing unwanted energy first prevents it from consuming headroom and generating disproportionate harmonics.
pairings.caution: Over-correction can starve the nonlinear stage and make the result smaller. Re-check the EQ after harmonics are generated.

insider_note: Documented behavior: Dry/Wet combined with Speed Stability can create chorusing. Crosstalk in Studio One Mix FX controls leakage across session channels, not only within one stereo insert.
avoid_when: Avoid it when the production needs obvious dropouts or decoupled damage—use Dirty Tape—or when timing modulation must be absent but peak density is wanted—use Overstayer M-A-S.

sources.title: Softube Tape user manual

name: Dirty Tape
comparative_edge: Choose Dirty Tape over Tape when wow, flutter, dropouts, darker low-speed color, and channel-to-channel instability are arrangement elements. Choose Tape for separable speed, crosstalk, noise, and machine types; choose OTO Biscuit for clocked digital reduction or Bad Speaker for a physical playback perspective.

advanced_moves.setup: On a static loop, set Dirt to minimum, Stereo Mode to Normal, and match Output before raising Drive.
advanced_moves.action: Find the distortion density with Drive alone, then return Drive slightly and raise Dirt until mechanical motion contributes as much as the saturation. Re-match after each stage.
advanced_moves.listen_for: You should be able to identify harmonic thickening and transport damage as two separate contributions; stop when dropouts erase the loop's groove anchor.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: Drive increases tape distortion, while Dirt is a macro for wow, flutter, dropouts, crosstalk, and lower-speed coloration.

advanced_moves.setup: On a stereo effects return rather than the dry source, switch from Normal to De-coupled after setting a moderate Dirt amount.
advanced_moves.action: Automate Dirt into transitions and compare coupled versus independent channel variation. Narrow the return downstream if the center wanders too far.
advanced_moves.listen_for: The return should breathe wider at transitions while the dry signal preserves pitch and center; avoid random image jumps on featured notes.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: De-coupled mode allows wow, flutter, and dropout variations to differ between left and right channels.

use_cases.application: Build distortion with Drive, introduce Dirt separately for motion, and keep the dry keys outside the insert so note attacks remain stable.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: Its two macros separate nonlinear density from compound mechanical wear more clearly than a generic lo-fi preset.

use_cases.application: Automate De-coupled Dirt upward across a transition while lowering the high cut, then return abruptly to a stable dry scene.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: Independent-channel transport defects create temporal and spatial deterioration that Bad Speaker's static device responses do not.

insider_note: Documented behavior: Dirt at maximum also applies coloration associated with low tape speed; at minimum it corresponds to high speed. It is not a modulation-depth control with otherwise constant tone.
avoid_when: Avoid it for subtle mastering glue, separately tuned crosstalk/noise, or repeatable wow rate; Tape exposes those decisions more cleanly.

sources.title: Softube Dirty Tape user manual

name: Harmonics Analog Saturation Processor
comparative_edge: Choose Harmonics over Saturation Knob when the nonlinear family, pre-emphasis, filters, blend, and post-distortion dynamics need separate control. Choose Overstayer M-A-S for hardware-specific peak bending and emphasis profiles, or Weiss Exciter when additive, frequency-targeted harmonics with minimal fundamental/EQ change are the priority.

advanced_moves.setup: On a kick, choose the least intrusive Drive Type, leave Drive at minimum or near-minimum, switch Dynamics on, and level-match the plug-in output.
advanced_moves.action: Treat Dynamics as the main processor: move it counterclockwise for a denser, rounder hit or clockwise for more front-edge separation. Only add Drive afterward if the kick actually needs overt saturation.
advanced_moves.listen_for: Counterclockwise should pull body and low-level detail forward like colorful compression; clockwise should make the attack separate without the click becoming detached.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: Dynamics analyzes the waveform before distortion and reconstructs or suppresses its movement, so the control can behave like a colored compressor/expander even when saturation is not the goal.

advanced_moves.setup: For a full-range source, duplicate Harmonics in series at low drive rather than pushing one full-band instance.
advanced_moves.action: Use the first instance's filters and Character to color the lower region with one Type, and the second to treat the upper region with another. Match each stage before judging the chain.
advanced_moves.listen_for: Low and high regions should acquire distinct textures without a single shared clipping ceiling flattening the whole source.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: Each Drive Type has tailored pre-distortion Character filtering, and serial low-drive stages can generate different harmonic structures in different spectral regions.

use_cases.application: Keep Drive at minimum or near-minimum and use Dynamics alone as a one-knob colored transient shaper: left for density and weight, right for greater attack contrast.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: Its pre-distortion envelope analysis gives a different, more nonlinear-feeling result than a conventional attack/sustain shaper.

use_cases.application: Use Character to focus drive on the useful register, then restore clocked attack with clockwise Dynamics rather than simply lowering Drive.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: Its dynamics reconstruction separates transient preservation from harmonic density, which Saturation Knob cannot.

use_cases.application: Treat lower and upper bands with two low-drive instances using different Types, preserving pick attack on the upper stage with Dynamics.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: Multiple nonlinear families, filters, and reconstruction allow controlled division of weight and grind without a separate multiband saturator.

pairings.goal: Remove drive-dominating excess before adding Harmonics Analog Saturation Processor.
pairings.order: Equalizers → Harmonics Analog Saturation Processor
pairings.setup: High-pass or make one restrained corrective cut first, level-match, then raise the color stage until the intended harmonics or peak bending appear.
pairings.why_it_works: Nonlinear processors respond to incoming level by frequency, so removing unwanted energy first prevents it from consuming headroom and generating disproportionate harmonics.
pairings.caution: Over-correction can starve the nonlinear stage and make the result smaller. Re-check the EQ after harmonics are generated.

insider_note: Producer practice: the catalog's sleeper move is to ignore overt saturation and use Dynamics as a colorful compressor/expander, especially on kicks. Softube documents the pre-distortion analysis and envelope reconstruction; the Drive-minimum application is a producer technique, not an official preset recipe.
avoid_when: Avoid it when one protected-band macro is enough—Saturation Knob is faster—or when the goal is only newly generated, precisely targeted harmonics—use Weiss Exciter.

sources.title: Softube Harmonics Analog Saturation Processor user manual
Bobby Owsinski: Softube Harmonics production review

name: Saturation Knob
comparative_edge: Choose it over Harmonics when speed and one protected spectral extreme are more valuable than choosing a distortion family or rebuilding dynamics. Choose Harmonics for filters, Character, Dry/Wet, THD metering, and transient control; choose Overstayer M-A-S when subtle peak bending with auto gain is the job.

advanced_moves.setup: On a bass source, duplicate to a parallel bus, high-pass that bus if the host permits, and set Saturation Knob to Keep Low.
advanced_moves.action: Drive until upper harmonics make the bass readable on small speakers, then blend under the clean track and verify the fundamental in mono.
advanced_moves.listen_for: Pitch should translate at low playback level while the original sub envelope remains stable; stop if the parallel path produces fizzy note edges.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: Keep Low applies more saturation to higher frequencies, preserving the lower region relative to Neutral mode.

advanced_moves.setup: On bright percussion, set Keep High and begin from no saturation with output matched downstream.
advanced_moves.action: Raise the knob until snare or body thickens beneath the cymbal band, then automate bypass for sections that need unprocessed transient contrast.
advanced_moves.listen_for: Lower percussion body should gain density while hats retain definition; reject settings that turn the complete bus dull.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: Keep High biases saturation toward lower frequencies so the high-frequency material remains comparatively intact.

use_cases.application: Use Keep High to densify kick and snare beneath cymbals, then blend the bus rather than driving the full kit insert.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: The three-position spectral bias reaches a useful protected-top parallel sound faster than configuring Harmonics.

use_cases.application: Use Neutral as a waveshaper to introduce harmonics, then control the resulting brightness with a later filter or the arrangement.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: Its simple clipping stage can turn spectrally sparse waveforms into audible overtone material without tape motion or speaker coloration.

pairings.goal: Remove drive-dominating excess before adding Saturation Knob.
pairings.order: Equalizers → Saturation Knob
pairings.setup: High-pass or make one restrained corrective cut first, level-match, then raise the color stage until the intended harmonics or peak bending appear.
pairings.why_it_works: Nonlinear processors respond to incoming level by frequency, so removing unwanted energy first prevents it from consuming headroom and generating disproportionate harmonics.
pairings.caution: Over-correction can starve the nonlinear stage and make the result smaller. Re-check the EQ after harmonics are generated.

insider_note: Documented behavior: the labels describe what is preserved. Keep Low saturates the higher portion more; Keep High saturates the lower portion more. Reading them as the processed band reverses the intended choice.
avoid_when: Avoid it when precise level matching, blend, filtering, or transient recovery must live inside the plugin; Harmonics supplies those controls.

sources.title: Softube Saturation Knob for Modular user manual

name: Overstayer M-A-S
comparative_edge: Choose standard M-A-S over Extended when six musically constrained emphasis profiles are faster than drawing a four-band emphasis curve. Choose Extended for exact spectral targeting; choose Harmonics for multiple analog-family models and dynamics reconstruction, or Tape when speed, crosstalk, and transport behavior are part of the sound.

advanced_moves.setup: On a track or bus, enable Auto Gain, set Mix fully wet, choose Classic M-A-S, and raise Input until the first saturation LED responds.
advanced_moves.action: Cycle all six Emphasis Types, re-adjusting Input each time to equalize the amount of saturation before selecting by tone. Restore parallel balance only after choosing.
advanced_moves.listen_for: Judge which region bends first and how steady versus transient material reacts; reject a mode that wins only because it is driven harder.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: Emphasis changes the operating range and frequency weighting before the M-A-S stages, so equal Input settings do not create equal saturation.

advanced_moves.setup: On a vocal or bright instrument that dulls as peaks bend, establish the desired Input and Mix with Dual and 2nd off.
advanced_moves.action: Engage Dual, then 2nd separately, retaining the smallest addition that restores clarity. Revisit Emphasis Type before adding top EQ downstream.
advanced_moves.listen_for: Presence should return as harmonic energy without sibilance becoming brittle or the fundamental losing weight.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: Dual and 2nd add more second harmonics and brighten the distorted result rather than applying a conventional high-frequency boost.

use_cases.context: Dance pop — Drum and instrument buses
use_cases.application: Use low-drive M-A-S across several buses with source-specific Emphasis Types, re-matching Input whenever the type changes.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: The standard profiles make cumulative peak bending faster to distribute than building a custom Extended curve on every bus.

use_cases.application: Compare Classic and Bass Distortion at equal LED activity, then add Dual only if the bent bass loses audibility above the fundamental.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: Its emphasis profiles decide which spectral regions clip while the broad M-A-S operating range can bend peaks without compressor release motion.

pairings.goal: Remove drive-dominating excess before adding Overstayer M-A-S.
pairings.order: Equalizers → Overstayer M-A-S
pairings.setup: High-pass or make one restrained corrective cut first, level-match, then raise the color stage until the intended harmonics or peak bending appear.
pairings.why_it_works: Nonlinear processors respond to incoming level by frequency, so removing unwanted energy first prevents it from consuming headroom and generating disproportionate harmonics.
pairings.caution: Over-correction can starve the nonlinear stage and make the result smaller. Re-check the EQ after harmonics are generated.

insider_note: Documented behavior: the first meter LED marks where bending begins, but low-order harmonic color exists below that point. 'No LED' is not necessarily a null-processing state.
avoid_when: Avoid standard M-A-S when a specific emphasis frequency or cutoff must be set; use M-A-S Extended. Avoid it for time instability or tape noise.

sources.title: Softube Overstayer M-A-S user manual

name: Overstayer M-A-S Extended
comparative_edge: Choose Extended over standard M-A-S when the saturation must be aimed at exact regions with a four-band emphasis EQ and resonant pre-filters. Choose standard for faster repeatable profiles across many tracks; choose Drawmer 1976 when saturation and stereo width must be independently controlled in three explicit crossover bands.

advanced_moves.setup: On a full-range bus, enable Emphasis, set filters wide, Auto Gain on, disengage Compensation for the target band, and establish low-level bending with Input before moving the EQ.
advanced_moves.action: Boost the pre-emphasis band feeding the target into saturation, then adjust its independent outer-ring post control toward the original tonal balance. Compare with the same apparent EQ but less Input.
advanced_moves.listen_for: The target region should gain harmonic density while the final broad spectrum stays close to bypass; reject a move that is only audible as EQ.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: Extended exposes the pre/post emphasis shaping that the standard version packages into fixed profiles, separating what drives from what is heard after.

advanced_moves.setup: For a bass-heavy or harsh source, engage only the pre-saturation HPF or LPF with resonance at minimum.
advanced_moves.action: Move the cutoff until the vulnerable extreme stops driving the stage, then add only enough Resonance to restore energy at the boundary. Re-set Input after filtering.
advanced_moves.listen_for: The protected extreme should stay cleaner while the cutoff area remains connected; stop if resonance becomes a new note or whistle.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: The 12 dB/octave resonant filters precede saturation, changing both the driven spectrum and the harmonics subsequently generated.

use_cases.application: Use pre/post emphasis to make the middle distort while returning lows and highs near the original balance, then blend beneath the clean mix.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: It offers continuous control over the spectral drive/de-emphasis relationship that standard M-A-S only approximates with profiles.

use_cases.application: High-pass before saturation, emphasize a chosen presence zone, and use filter resonance sparingly to keep the effect voiced around the singer.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: The pre-saturation filters and editable emphasis can isolate vocal color more precisely than Harmonics' global Character control.

insider_note: Documented behavior: the hardware's emergency op-amp safety-clipping circuit was deliberately omitted from both plug-ins after consultation with Overstayer. Very hot digital input can therefore reach a different final failure mode than the hardware.
avoid_when: Avoid Extended when one of the six standard profiles already fits; its extra pre/post and resonant controls add ways to mis-level the comparison.

sources.title: Softube Overstayer M-A-S user manual

name: Drawmer 1976 Three Band Saturator
comparative_edge: Choose Drawmer 1976 over Harmonics when the production decision is explicitly low/mid/high saturation plus independent stereo width. Choose Harmonics for nonlinear families and transient reconstruction without crossovers; choose M-A-S Extended for continuous pre/post emphasis and peak bending rather than three recombined bands.

advanced_moves.setup: On a full mix or drum-and-bass bus, set both crossovers around musical role boundaries, all Width controls centered, and Mono Check available.
advanced_moves.action: Keep Low Width at or near mono, widen Mid and High in separate passes, then toggle Mono Check after each. Add saturation only after the stereo architecture translates.
advanced_moves.listen_for: Sub energy and the phantom center should remain fixed while upper ambience expands; mono should preserve impact rather than exposing a scooped band.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: Each crossover band has independent width before recombination, so stereo expansion can be limited to regions that tolerate side energy.

advanced_moves.setup: For a source whose midrange needs density but whose extremes are already controlled, bypass or zero all three saturators and set crossovers by soloed musical roles.
advanced_moves.action: Drive Mid first, then add smaller Low or High amounts only if the recombined source feels disconnected. Revisit crossovers after saturation because generated harmonics may cross the chosen boundaries.
advanced_moves.listen_for: Mid density should increase without a seam at either crossover or a softer sub transient.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: The signal is split before three independent nonlinear stages, so crossover placement decides which fundamentals generate harmonics in each processor.

use_cases.context: Drum and bass — Bass and drum master bus
use_cases.application: Keep the low band narrow and lightly driven, saturate the mid growl, and widen only upper bands while checking mono.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: Its three parallel width and saturation zones protect sub localization more directly than a full-band saturator.

use_cases.context: Orchestral trailer — Percussion and low-brass stem
use_cases.application: Use light low/mid saturation for scale, leaving high saturation restrained while widening only the upper room contribution.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: Frequency-specific density and width can enlarge a composite stem without putting cymbal air and low impacts through the same nonlinear stage.

insider_note: Engineering inference from the documented split-band architecture: crossover changes after drive is set alter not only band level but which fundamentals feed each nonlinear stage, so always re-evaluate saturation after moving a crossover.
avoid_when: Avoid it when crossover phase/partitioning is undesirable or when one continuous full-band transfer curve is the goal; use Harmonics or Overstayer M-A-S.

Softube Drawmer 1976 Three Band Saturator product page

name: OTO Biscuit 8-bit Effects
comparative_edge: Choose Biscuit over Dirty Tape for clock-rate reduction, individual bit mutation, a multimode analog-modeled filter, and tempo-capable digital effects. Choose Dirty Tape for continuous mechanical instability, or Bad Speaker when the illusion should be a physical playback device rather than exposed data conversion.

advanced_moves.setup: Set all eight bits on, Brain off, Naked at unity, Dressed low, and Clock high enough that the source remains recognizable.
advanced_moves.action: Mute or invert LSBs one at a time before touching higher bits; lower Clock only after a useful bit pattern emerges. Keep a limiter or conservative monitoring level downstream.
advanced_moves.listen_for: Low-order changes should add texture while preserving rhythm and pitch; stop before an MSB change creates uncontrolled level or replaces the source with static.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: LSBs create subtler changes than MSBs, whose inversion or removal radically changes the 8-bit sample value and can produce loud noise.

advanced_moves.setup: On a drum fill or synth sequence, establish the core bit/Clock sound, engage Brain's Step effect, and tempo-reference the pattern.
advanced_moves.action: Sequence filter movement while using the analog-modeled multimode Filter for the final bandwidth. Blend Naked and Dressed rather than filtering the dry path externally.
advanced_moves.listen_for: Rhythmic degradation should reinforce the phrase grid while transients remain locatable in the dry component.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: One Brain effect can run alongside sample-rate reduction and bit mutation, followed by a resonant low-, band-, or high-pass filter and parallel mixer.

use_cases.application: Develop an LSB-first bit pattern, lower Clock for bandwidth, then animate the Step filter for one resampled transition.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: It combines data-level mutation, clock artifacts, rhythmic effect, and analog-style filtering in one repeatable digital instrument.

use_cases.application: Blend Dressed beneath Naked, automate one or two bit inversions, and use Pitch as the single active Brain effect for phrase-end mutations.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: Individual bit states create discrete timbral events that Dirty Tape's continuous Dirt macro cannot reproduce.

insider_note: Documented behavior: the bit switches have three states—on, muted, and inverted—and the most significant bit is the most drastic. Shift-click changes all switches to the same state, which can cause an abrupt full-pattern jump.
avoid_when: Avoid it on uncontrolled full-level masters or when smooth analog degradation is required; bit inversions can be very loud, and Dirty Tape is the safer continuous-motion choice.

sources.title: Softube OTO Biscuit 8-bit Effects user manual

name: Bad Speaker
comparative_edge: Choose Bad Speaker over OTO Biscuit when the cue should read as a radio, cassette deck, or speaker-in-room rather than abstract bit reduction. Choose Dirty Tape for time-varying wear and dropouts; choose Bad Speaker for repeatable device response, breakup, width, and dry/wet placement.

advanced_moves.setup: On a mono source, audition all three Speaker modes at low Drive, Width fully mono, and Mix fully wet before adding stereo processing.
advanced_moves.action: Choose the physical response first, then increase Width until the treated component separates from the dry center. Blend Mix last and verify mono.
advanced_moves.listen_for: The effect should widen around a stable core; reject settings where mono loses the intended device tone or the source's location becomes ambiguous.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: Speaker selection, nonlinear Drive, Width, and parallel Mix are independent decisions; widening before choosing the model can disguise the actual response.

advanced_moves.setup: For dialogue, vocal, or drum perspective, place Bad Speaker on a parallel bus and begin with Cassette Deck or Hi-Fi rather than the most restricted Portable Radio.
advanced_moves.action: Use Tone to fit the return behind the clean source, drive until the speaker character becomes identifiable, then automate the return send rather than changing Drive every section.
advanced_moves.listen_for: The clean source should remain intelligible while the return adds location and grit; avoid comb-like hollowness at intermediate Mix values.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: The dedicated dry/wet and modeled speaker responses let device perspective be layered without forcing the direct signal through the same bandwidth restriction.

use_cases.context: Boom bap — Snare and percussion parallel
use_cases.application: Use Cassette Deck for mid bite, add moderate Drive, and narrow Width until the dirty layer reinforces rather than smears the center.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: Its measured device response supplies resonant speaker breakup that an EQ plus Saturation Knob would not recreate as one behavior.

use_cases.application: Use Hi-Fi Speaker for a room perspective, automate Width and send level, and reserve Portable Radio for brief contrast events.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: Three repeatable physical perspectives make spatial storytelling easier than Dirty Tape's random transport damage.

insider_note: Documented behavior: Bad Speaker can occupy either Shape or Drive in Console 1 and can be placed freely in Amp Room Studio mode, enabling placement before or after other nonlinear modules as a meaningful tone change.
avoid_when: Avoid it when exact bit depth, sample clock, or moving tape defects define the effect; use OTO Biscuit or Dirty Tape respectively.

name: Empirical Labs Professor Punch-Knuckles
comparative_edge: Choose Professor over Mike-E Comp when you want its three ELI nonlinearities without configuring a full preamp/compressor. Choose Mike-E for controllable attack, ratio, external sidechain, and separate preamp staging; choose Harmonics when transient reconstruction and non-ELI distortion families are more important than Toasty, Crunchy, or Distress.

advanced_moves.setup: At moderate gain-compensated Drive, compare Toasty, Crunchy, and Distress with post Low Cut, Tone, and High Cut neutral.
advanced_moves.action: Select the transfer behavior first, then compare XFRM, Wide, and Tape at that same moderate amount. Add post filters only after both stages are chosen.
advanced_moves.listen_for: You should hear mode-specific spectral emphasis before heavy distortion makes them converge; reject a choice that is only louder or darker after filtering.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: Distortion selects the nonlinear circuit, while Mode changes its tonal emphasis; Mode differences are documented as clearer at moderate drive.

advanced_moves.setup: On a parallel drum or vocal bus, select Distress, Mix fully wet, and begin below 3 dB of gain reduction.
advanced_moves.action: Increase Drive into roughly 3–5 dB of reduction, then lower Mix to restore dry attacks. Use the post filters to keep the crushed layer out of vulnerable extremes.
advanced_moves.listen_for: The source should sit forward with controlled peaks while dry transients remain legible; stop before room noise or breath becomes a continuous floor.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: Distress is the Distressor/Mike-E compressor circuit at its fastest aggressive setting, while Mix blends the pre-effect dry signal back in.

use_cases.application: Use Distress for several dB of fast reduction, blend back dry transients, and high-pass the crushed layer after distortion.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: It reaches the ELI compression-distortion behavior faster than building the equivalent Mike-E chain.

use_cases.application: Compare Crunchy and Toasty at moderate THD, select Tape emphasis if top-edge breakup should lead, then automate Mix between phrases.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: Three ELI circuit types plus separate emphasis and post filtering make vocal aggression repeatable without a full multistage processor.

insider_note: Documented behavior: the meter changes meaning by distortion type—THD percentage for Toasty and Crunchy, gain reduction for Distress. A visually identical reading is not the same measurement across modes.
avoid_when: Avoid it when compressor timing, external sidechain, or a clean preamp state must be controlled explicitly; Mike-E Comp is the fuller ELI tool.

name: Empirical Labs Mike-E Comp
comparative_edge: Choose Mike-E over Professor Punch-Knuckles when the preamp, high-pass, attack, ratio, CompSat timing, emphasis, external sidechain, and parallel mix must be engineered as stages. Choose Professor for rapid ELI color; choose a Softube FET compressor when saturation should not be frequency-dependent CompSat behavior.

advanced_moves.setup: Set the preamp CLEAN, CompSat Ratio to 1:1, Mix fully processed, and watch the Warm/Toasty indicators rather than compressor gain reduction.
advanced_moves.action: Raise Drive until Warm remains active and Toasty catches peaks, then compare HF emphasis for earlier high-frequency clipping. Follow with another compressor only after output matching.
advanced_moves.listen_for: Peaks should flatten by a small amount while body gains heat; HF emphasis should soften buildup without making the source dull.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: At 1:1, CompSat's soft-clipping remains while conventional compression is removed; emphasis changes which frequencies hit saturation first.

advanced_moves.setup: On drums or bass, set CompSat for only 2–3 dB of reduction and establish the envelope before adding preamp gain.
advanced_moves.action: Toggle the preamp from CLEAN and raise its Gain separately, then compensate Output. If attack blurs, reduce preamp distortion instead of changing CompSat timing first.
advanced_moves.listen_for: Preamp grit should add a first layer of texture while CompSat continues controlling the same envelope; the BAD LED should not remain lit from unintended clipping.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: Mike-E has a distinct preamp distortion stage before the frequency-dependent CompSat circuit, so their contributions can be isolated.

use_cases.application: Use 1:1 soft clipping with HF emphasis to shave harsh peaks, then add restrained CompSat reduction and parallel Mix for stable density.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: It combines ELI preamp, frequency-dependent clipping, compression, and emphasis with control that Professor intentionally hides.

use_cases.application: Set the CompSat envelope first, then add a separate preamp-distortion layer and use Mix to retain the original hit onset.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: The serial preamp and CompSat stages can shape texture and decay independently before parallel recovery.

pairings.goal: Build a complete ELI tracking chain with filtering/de-essing before CompSat compression and color.
pairings.order: Empirical Labs Lil FrEQ → Empirical Labs Mike-E Comp
pairings.setup: High-pass and solve resonances in Lil FrEQ, place its DS for needed sibilance control, then set Mike-E preamp and CompSat from the conditioned signal.
pairings.why_it_works: Lil FrEQ removes spectral triggers before Mike-E's frequency-dependent saturation/compression; Softube's Trak Pak combines these product roles in this channel-strip order.
pairings.caution: Heavy high-frequency limiting can starve Mike-E emphasis and dull the chain. Re-set CompSat drive after every input-EQ change.

insider_note: Documented behavior: the BAD LED indicates clipping somewhere that was not intended to clip; it is different from the Warm and Toasty indicators used to judge the designed CompSat saturation range.
avoid_when: Avoid it when you only need quick ELI saturation—Professor is faster—or when clean, transparent level control is the assignment.

name: Empirical Labs Lil FrEQ
comparative_edge: Choose Lil FrEQ over Equalizers when the ELI analog path, steep resonant high-pass, four overlapping parametrics, and level-independent de-ess/HF limiter are one tracking-style chain. Choose Equalizers for multiple dynamic bands and M/S sidechain work; choose Mike-E when saturation/compression, not high-frequency containment, is the center of the job.

advanced_moves.setup: On a vocal, set the broad shelves and parametrics for the desired bright tone before engaging the DS section.
advanced_moves.action: Compare DS pre-EQ and post-EQ. Use post-EQ when the new boost should trigger control; use pre-EQ when de-essing should remain independent of later tone shaping.
advanced_moves.listen_for: Sibilants should return to the intended level while vowels keep the added brightness; reject constant reduction or lisping.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: The DS block can be moved before or after EQ, changing whether boosted high-frequency energy reaches its detector.

advanced_moves.setup: For a source whose harshness grows with level rather than only on sibilants, select HF Limit instead of De-ess and begin around the offending range.
advanced_moves.action: Set the level-dependent threshold to react only on loud phrases, then drive Input slightly harder to audition the documented tape-like increase in high-frequency smoothing.
advanced_moves.listen_for: Loud events should darken gently while quiet articulation remains; stop if every phrase loses air or the BAD LED indicates unintended clipping.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: HF Limit uses a normal level-dependent soft-knee limiter, unlike the de-esser's level-independent high-versus-low comparison.

use_cases.application: Brighten with shelves/parametrics, place DS post-EQ, and choose level-independent de-ess so only spectral imbalance triggers control.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: Its movable DS block lets one analog-modeled chain establish brightness and contain the exact excess that brightness creates.

use_cases.application: Use the 18 dB/octave high-pass conservatively, then tune De-ess toward intermittent finger-slide squeaks rather than the entire top end.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: The level-independent detector can catch spectral squeaks that a conventional threshold-based compressor may miss as performance level changes.

pairings.goal: Turn Lil FrEQ's corrective and HF-control stages into the front end of an ELI compression/saturation channel.
pairings.order: Empirical Labs Lil FrEQ → Empirical Labs Mike-E Comp
pairings.setup: Remove subs and resonances, choose DS pre/post EQ, level-match, then use Mike-E for peak shaving, envelope, and controlled analog color.
pairings.why_it_works: Frequency cleanup keeps unwanted regions from dominating CompSat, while Mike-E supplies the dynamics and distortion Lil FrEQ does not; Trak Pak documents the combined roles.
pairings.caution: Avoid large Lil FrEQ boosts into Mike-E unless the resulting frequency-biased compression is intentional.

insider_note: Documented behavior: plugin Bypass does not bypass the Input and Output volume controls. For valid A/B tests, use section bypasses or verify gain staging rather than assuming global Bypass is a wire.
avoid_when: Avoid it for several independent moving resonances or M/S dynamic repair; Equalizers is more flexible. Its steep high-pass also deserves caution during tracking.

name: Tube-Tech Blue Tone
comparative_edge: Choose Blue Tone over Tape or Harmonics when the desired polish is actually coordinated three-band optical compression, de-essing, PE/ME equalization, and possibly width—not simple saturation. Choose Tape for machine color without macro compression, Harmonics for explicit nonlinear control, or Tube-Tech SMC 2B when crossover and band timing must be exposed.

advanced_moves.setup: Set Amount to zero, Low/High Band neutral, Dry/Wet fully wet, and audition every Mode on the same source before raising Amount.
advanced_moves.action: Select by the mode's movement and spectral priorities, then raise Amount toward its designed 50% center while watching gain reduction. Correct only afterward with the post-compression Low/High controls.
advanced_moves.listen_for: Compression should solve a source-specific problem before the tone knobs flatter it; reject modes that sound exciting only because they are wider or brighter.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: Mode changes hidden crossovers, ratios, timing, de-essing, EQ, and sometimes width; Amount moves several of those parameters together.

advanced_moves.setup: On drums, guitars, or a mix bus, choose the closest Mode and drive Amount beyond the subtle range to hear its full envelope.
advanced_moves.action: Back Amount down until gain reduction is useful, then reduce Dry/Wet to reintroduce uncompressed transients. Re-trim post-compression Low/High bands only after the blend is stable.
advanced_moves.listen_for: The wet path should supply density and tone while the dry path restores hit onset; avoid a phasey or detached parallel balance.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: Blue Tone's Dry/Wet blends the coordinated multiband compression/EQ result with the unprocessed signal, preserving transients without changing hidden timing.

use_cases.application: Compare Vocal Clarify and Vocal Focus from Amount zero, choose by gain-reduction behavior, then use post High Band only after de-essing is correct.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: Its vocal modes coordinate multiband optical compression, de-essing, and Tube-Tech EQ faster than assembling separate Blue-series stages.

use_cases.application: Drive Drum Bus mode until glue is obvious, back Amount down, and use Dry/Wet to restore transient contrast before touching Low/High tone.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: The macro controls a tuned multiband envelope and tone recipe, not just the harmonic density available from Tape or Harmonics.

insider_note: Documented behavior: Low and High Band controls apply up to ±6 dB after compression, and their cutoff points change with Mode. Identical knob positions across modes do not describe identical curves.
avoid_when: Avoid it when exact crossover, attack, release, ratio, or saturation behavior must be known; use SMC 2B/Equalizers or a dedicated saturator instead.

name: Weiss Exciter
comparative_edge: Choose Weiss Exciter over Harmonics when you want additive harmonics targeted by independent input/output bands, adaptive level behavior, M/S width, and minimal fundamental-EQ shift. Choose Harmonics for full-waveform analog-family distortion and dynamics reconstruction; choose Weiss EQ MP when a static high-frequency lift is sufficient and no new overtones are needed.

advanced_moves.setup: Enable Adaptive and Mastering, choose a harmonic Mode, and define a narrow Pre target band around the fundamentals you want to excite.
advanced_moves.action: Place the Post band at least an octave above the Pre high-pass region, raise Harmonics while monitoring the wet/difference signal, then widen Post only if useful overtones are being excluded.
advanced_moves.listen_for: The added signal should sound related to the source rather than like filtered hiss; bypass should remove vibrancy without collapsing the original tonal balance.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: Generated harmonics occur above their fundamentals, and independent pre/post filters separate what creates harmonics from which harmonics reach the output.

advanced_moves.setup: On a stereo master or ambience bus, establish a linked stereo setting, then switch to M/S with Width neutral and channels ganged.
advanced_moves.action: Reduce wet Width or process Side more conservatively if excitation exaggerates ambience; compare minimum-phase and linear-phase only after the harmonic balance is stable.
advanced_moves.listen_for: Crispness should rise without cymbals pulling outward or the phantom center narrowing; check mono for unchanged dry integrity.
advanced_moves.why_it_works: Width changes only the wet contribution. Minimum-phase mode phase-compensates the dry path for coherent summing; linear-phase mode leaves that dry path unprocessed.

use_cases.application: Use Adaptive Mastering mode, target fundamentals below the desired sparkle, and monitor only the generated band before blending subtly.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: It can add level-stable overtones with reduced fundamental leakage instead of relying on a broad EQ shelf or full-waveform saturation.

use_cases.context: Ambient techno — Reverb and texture bus
use_cases.application: Generate harmonics from a bounded midrange Pre band, constrain their Post band, and reduce wet Side width if the return becomes diffuse.
use_cases.why_this_plugin: Independent target/output bands and wet-width control provide more spatial discipline than Harmonics' full-signal drive.

pairings.goal: Set transparent static balance first, then add bounded harmonics instead of another high shelf.
pairings.order: Weiss EQ MP → Weiss Exciter
pairings.setup: Complete cuts and broad balance in EQ MP, match output, then select Exciter Pre fundamentals and Post harmonic range while monitoring the wet contribution.
pairings.why_it_works: EQ MP changes existing spectrum; Exciter adds new overtones on a parallel path and can reduce fundamental leakage in Mastering mode.
pairings.caution: Do not duplicate brightness with an EQ shelf and excitation. Match loudness and check fatigue at low monitor level.

insider_note: Documented behavior: in minimum-phase mode the internal dry/wet paths are phase-compensated to prevent cancellation without linear-phase latency. Linear phase is optional, not required for coherent parallel blending.
avoid_when: Avoid it when obvious clipping, low-frequency thickening, or transient rounding is the goal; Harmonics, Overstayer M-A-S, or Tape is the more direct Softube choice.
